name: v3 Comic panel, tube collar, potato duty
medium: photographed panel from a newsprint comic book; collar closed up to the helmet; mundane chore
prompt: Photograph of a single panel from a 1940s ten-cent war comic book, printed on yellowed newsprint, shot flat under warm lamp light. A figure in an olive drab greatcoat sits on an upturned crate outside a canvas tent, peeling a potato over a tin bucket with thick leather-gloved hands. The greatcoat has a tall stiff collar buttoned all the way up, standing like a tube to the rim of the helmet, with a wool scarf wound inside it. The head is a round American steel helmet resting on that collar like a lid on a jar, and the narrow slot between the helmet brim and the collar top is one flat solid black shape, pure black ink with a hard edge. Bold black brush outlines, flat four-colour inks, coarse visible halftone dots, olive, khaki, brick red and pale yellow. Empty white speech balloon above, paper grain, slight page curl.

name: v3 Ink cartoon, tube collar, tin cup
medium: frontline one-panel gag cartoon; collar closed up to the helmet
prompt: Single-panel 1940s frontline newspaper gag cartoon, black brush ink and grease crayon on rough off-white newsprint. A figure sits on an ammunition crate in a muddy foxhole, squared to the viewer, thick knitted gloves on both hands wrapped around a steaming tin cup. The heavy wool overcoat has a tall stiff collar buttoned to the top with a scarf wound inside it, the collar standing like a tube up to the helmet rim. The head is a round American steel helmet resting on that collar like a lid on a jar, and the narrow slot between the helmet brim and the collar top is filled edge to edge with one flat pool of solid black ink. Heavy slashing brush strokes, deep spotted blacks, scratchy crayon tone on the mud and sky, sagging tired posture. Wide blank strip of paper below the drawing reserved for a typed caption. Slight ink bleed, visible paper fibre.
